citation: E. Escoto et al., "Polarization-Based Contrast Enhancement during Spectral Broadening in a Multi-Pass Cell", CLEO 2024, paper SF2O.8
fullTextRead: Only the abstract and the key points of the figures as supplied by the owner (the licensed PDF is not in the repository and is never copied). Every figure value below is read off by the owner's description.
topic: nonlinear ellipse rotation in a multi-pass cell: efficiency and temporal contrast versus the two quarter-wave plate angles

referenceNumbers.value: QWP1 x QWP2 angles over [-50, 50] deg; polariser behind
(1) energy through the polariser, normalised to its peak; (2) contrast improvement at +2 ps, peak over intensity at +2 ps, output vs input
efficiency ~0 in a tilted ellipse along theta1 = theta2; maxima near (theta2, theta1) = (-30, +35) and (+30, -35) deg; symmetric under (theta1, theta2) -> (-theta1, -theta2)
contrast improvement only on theta1 = theta2, from ~0 at the origin to ~8-9 (log10) near +-45 deg
along theta1 = theta2: 0.55 at 3 deg, maximum 1 at ~10 deg (P1), minimum ~0.47 at ~26 deg, second maximum ~0.62 at ~35 deg, ~0.4 at 40 deg (P2), 0 at ~44 deg
P1 spectrum strongly modulated (~1015-1050 nm); P2 smooth, single-lobed; P2 pulse much cleaner than P1 after compression

assumptions: The cell is NOT stated in the source used. Hypothesis: the multi-pass cell of Seidel et al., Laser Photon. Rev. 16, 2100268 (2022), arXiv:2105.05882 (~350 mm, ROC 200 mm, three 1 mm AR-coated fused-silica plates 3 cm apart, 31 round trips, 900 fs at 1030 nm; B tuned, ~10 rad in simulation, ~15 rad maximum in the experiment).

Model: 1-D plane wave; the cell is ONE fused-silica Kerr element (1 mm, constant beam) whose energy gives B = 10 rad for LINEAR light (circular light then sees 2/3 of it). Dispersion per round trip is taken as compensated (the 1 mm element's own GDD is ~19 fs2). Raman of silica on (engine default).
Input: 900 fs Gaussian at 1030 nm, linear along x. Polariser crossed (axis y). QWP2 angle is plotted with the sign that puts the dark ellipse along theta1 = theta2 (engine angle = -paper angle).

Input contrast at +2 ps is the analytic Gaussian value (8.8e5). The polariser and waveplates are ideal; the contrast improvement is then set by the sharpness of the linear null, not by an extinction ratio.
Values read off figures carry tolerances of a few degrees / 10-15 %.
